info.name: Supplier Master · Map Services (/api/vendors/{id})
info.description:
Supplier Master · Map Services — the supplier side of p2p_service_suppliers (same rows the Service screen's Map Supplier popup uses).

HOW TO RUN
1. Set collection variables: base_url (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8000/api), email, password.
2. 0. Auth › Login → stores {{token}} (Bearer auth for every request).
3. 1. Setup → fills soft_service_id, trackable_service_id, map_vendor_id, map_vendor_id_intl, material_vendor_id, currency from your data.
4. 2. Map Services → 3. Validation → 4. Cleanup. Or Run collection (Runner) top to bottom; every request has tests.

DATA NEEDED
• A Soft / Digital service with a GST % (Stage 1).
• A Trackable service.
• A supplier in India and one outside India whose Supplier Type is Soft Service Provider.
• A Material / Goods supplier.

ENDPOINTS
GET    /vendors/{id}/service-mappings        list (inactive included) + summary + meta
POST   /vendors/{id}/step/services           save the step — REPLACE-ALL (other active mappings of the supplier → inactive)
PATCH  /vendors/{id}/service-mappings/{map}  edit price / currency / exchange_rate / remarks
DELETE /vendors/{id}/service-mappings/{map}  soft unmap (status = inactive, row kept; mapping again revives the same row)

RULES (server-side)
• Supplier visible (404) and editable (403); service visible (422) and editable (403).
• Supplier type must serve the service type + classification (422). Material / Goods and FFD / Transporter serve no service.
• origin must match the supplier's country (422).
• Domestic: ₹ + the service's GST %; the service needs a GST % (422). International: currency × exchange_rate, no GST, inr_amount stored.
• Same service twice in one save (422).

Every request has a saved example response (Examples), captured from the real API. Full doc: docs/supplier/SUPPLIER_MAP_SERVICES_API.md

request.description: Sets {{token}} for every other request. Fill email / password in the collection variables first.

item.name: 1. Setup · fills every id automatically
item.description: Run these once after Login. Each request picks an id from your data and stores it in a collection variable. If one is missing, the test fails and says what to create — or set the variable by hand.

item.name: Soft / Digital service with a GST %

request.description: Picks the first Soft / Digital service that has a GST % (Domestic mappings need it) → {{soft_service_id}}.

exec: pm.test('a Soft / Digital service with a GST % exists (set GST in Stage 1)', () => pm.expect(s).to.be.an('object'));

request.description: Any Self-Consumable · Trackable service → {{trackable_service_id}}.

item.name: Domestic supplier that serves Soft / Digital

request.description: A supplier in India whose Supplier Type serves Soft / Digital (e.g. Soft Service Provider) → {{map_vendor_id}}.

exec: pm.test('a Domestic Soft Service Provider supplier exists', () => pm.expect(v).to.be.an('object'));
if (v) { pm.collectionVariables.set('map_vendor_id', v.id); console.log('map_vendor_id =', v.id, v.vendor_code, v.supplier_type); }

item.name: International supplier that serves Soft / Digital

request.description: A supplier outside India of the same type → {{map_vendor_id_intl}} and its currency → {{currency}}.

exec: pm.test('an International Soft Service Provider supplier exists', () => pm.expect(v).to.be.an('object'));

request.description: Any supplier whose type is Material / Goods (or another non-service type) → {{material_vendor_id}}.

item.name: 2. Map Services (happy path)
item.description: Run top to bottom. POST step/services is REPLACE-ALL: it maps the listed services and sets this supplier's OTHER active mappings inactive (never deleted). Use test suppliers, not live ones.
